anomalies.observed: Each isolated CAN transceiver has both ground pins connected to the same GND net, tying the logic and bus-side grounds together.
anomalies.expected: To provide the galvanic isolation specified for the CAN interfaces, each transceiver's logic-side and bus-side grounds must remain electrically separate.

evidence.quote: two isolated CAN buses (CAN0, CAN1), each driven by its own MCP2515 SPI CAN controller (U8, U9) through an isolated CAN transceiver (U11/companion)

anomalies.impact: The shared ground bypasses the transceivers' isolation barriers, so the CAN interfaces will not provide the intended galvanic isolation and may be vulnerable to ground loops or common-mode differences.

anomalies.observed: C46 is valued 22pF, while the three analogous capacitors C42, C44, and C45 are 22nF; C46's part metadata also identifies it as 22nF.
anomalies.expected: C46 should be 22nF to match the corresponding center-tap filter capacitors and its own listed part metadata.
anomalies.impact: If sourced or assembled according to the 22pF value, this branch's filtering will differ substantially from the other three; the design value also conflicts with the listed 22nF part.

parsed.summary: An anomaly is present: both isolated CAN transceivers have their logic-side and bus-side grounds shorted together, defeating galvanic isolation. C46 also has a 22pF value inconsistent with its 22nF part metadata and the other matching capacitors.
